angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 225,616 km at 8.08 pc = 0.37 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 123.7756 +/- 0.0329 mas (same row, RUWE 1.09): 8.08 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.3243 +/- 0.0044 solar radii from Weiner Mansfield et al. 2024, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of GJ 486 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024ApJ...975L..22W/abstract): 225,616 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.312 +/- 0.007 solar masses from Weiner Mansfield et al. 2024, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of GJ 486 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024ApJ...975L..22W/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3317 +/- 36 K from Weiner Mansfield et al. 2024, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of GJ 486 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024ApJ...975L..22W/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Weiner Mansfield et al. 2024, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of GJ 486 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024ApJ...975L..22W/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/gj-486.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.910, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
